# **I. Overview**

## **1\. Context Diagram**

The context diagram shows TuConnector as a single process and its interactions with five human actors and five external systems. Each external entity has two data flows: one into the system and one out of the system (the arrow head shows the direction). Compared with the initial draft, the Admin actor, the Guest actor, Email Service and Google OAuth were added to cover account verification, moderation and sign-in flow

![][image2]

*Image 1\. Context diagram TuConnector*

## **2\. User Requirements**

### **2.1 Introduction**

TuConnector is a web platform that acts as a trusted third party connecting tutors with parents who need tutoring for their children, and at the same time provides tutors with a teaching workspace and students with a learning dashboard.

**Business problem.** In Vietnam, parents usually find tutors through acquaintances, social-media groups or traditional tutoring centres. Information about tutors' qualifications is hard to verify, matching is manual and slow, payments are informal, and after hiring there is no shared place to manage schedules, materials, homework and progress. Tutors, on the other hand, juggle Zalo/Facebook groups, spreadsheets and calendars to run their classes.

**Product vision.** TuConnector provides (1) a marketplace with verified tutor profiles, tutoring requests, AI-assisted matching, Q\&A, hiring and secure online payment; (2) a tutor workspace for classrooms, group chats, schedules synchronised with Google Calendar, materials, assignments and an AI Teaching Assistant; and (3) dashboards for students and parents to follow learning progress.

**Scope of release 1.0:**

* Account management with email/Google sign-in for Parent, Tutor, Student and Admin.

* Tutor discovery: search, profiles, posts, public Q\&A and AI tutor suggestions.

* Hiring: tutoring requests, applications, direct hire requests, contracts and online payment with platform commission.

* Tutor workspace: classrooms, members, materials, assignments & grading, recurring schedule, Google Calendar sync, group chat and AI Teaching Assistant.

* Student dashboard and parent progress monitoring, feedback & rating.

* Administration: tutor verification, user management, moderation, master data and statistics.

*Out of scope: native mobile apps, built-in video conferencing (sessions use external meeting links such as Google Meet/Zoom), automatic payout to tutors' bank accounts (handled manually by Admin in release 1.0).*

**Constraints & assumptions:**

* Web application, responsive, Vietnamese/English UI; deployed on a cloud server with a relational database (SQL Server/PostgreSQL).

* Proposed stack: ReactJS front-end, ASP.NET Core Web API (or Node.js/Spring Boot) back-end, SignalR/Socket.IO for real-time features.

* External services: Google Gemini API (AI Provider), PayOS/VNPay (Payment Gateway), Google Calendar API & Google OAuth, SMTP/SendGrid (Email).

* Project effort is limited to 400 man-hours for a team of 5 members (≈ 80 hours per member, 10 weeks).

* Users have internet access and a valid email; tutors can provide identity/qualification documents.

### **2.2 Actors**

| \# | Actor | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | Guest | An unauthenticated visitor who can browse the landing page, search tutors, view public profiles and posts, and register an account. |
| 2 | Parent | A parent/guardian who needs tutoring for their child(ren). Posts tutoring requests, receives AI tutor suggestions, invites tutors or answers tutors who are interested, chats with tutors, can join classes, monitors children's progress and rates tutors. Parents use the platform free of charge. |
| 3 | Tutor | A tutor/teacher with a public profile. Manages posts, expresses interest in requests and answers invitations using connection credits (Free / Pro plan), and uses the optional workspace: classrooms, members, materials, AI-generated assignments, schedule and group chats. |
| 4 | Student | A learner who joins a tutor's classroom by invite link or join code. Uses the Student Dashboard to follow the schedule, do assignments, view results, request schedule changes and chat with the class. |
| 5 | Admin | The platform operator. Manages user accounts, moderates content and reports, configures plans and pricing (credits, AI quota, SMS reminders) and monitors system statistics. |

*Table 2\. Actors (5 human actors)*

**External systems (secondary / system actors):**

| External system | Role | Related UCs |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| AI Provider (e.g. Google Gemini API) | Generates AI output for three features: tutor suggestions for parents, request (post) suggestions for tutors and assignment generation. | UC09, UC13, UC26 |
| Payment Gateway (e.g. PayOS / VNPay) | Processes online payments for Pro plan subscriptions and credit packs (QR/bank/card) and returns the result via redirect and IPN webhook. | UC19 |
| Google Calendar API | Creates/updates/deletes calendar events for class sessions in users' Google Calendars. | UC28, UC30, UC31 |
| Email / SMS Service (SMTP / SendGrid, SMS gateway) | Sends verification, reset password and notification emails, and SMS session reminders for the Pro plan. | UC01, UC03, UC28, UC35 |
| Google OAuth | Authenticates users with a Google account (sign-in and calendar consent). | UC01, UC02, UC31 |

*Table 3\. External systems*

| UC02 | Authentication & Profile | Parent, Tutor, Student, Admin | Login | Allows a registered user to sign in with email/password or Google and be redirected to the dashboard of their role. |
| UC03 | Authentication & Profile | Parent, Tutor, Student | Forgot Password | Allows a user to reset a forgotten password through a one-time link/OTP sent to the registered email. |
| UC04 | Authentication & Profile | Parent, Tutor, Student, Admin | Change Password | Allows a logged-in user to change the password. |
| UC05 | Authentication & Profile | Parent, Tutor, Student, Admin | Manage Profile | One LinkedIn-style profile per user: the owner edits it in place and other users see the public view of the same page. Tutors add headline, subjects, grade levels, experience, education, achievements, hourly rate and availability; parents keep a short public profile (name, area, children's grades, active requests). |
| UC06 | Tutor Discovery & Q\&A | Guest, Parent | Search & Filter Tutors | Allows guests and parents to search tutors by keyword, subject, grade level, teaching mode, area, price range and rating. |
| UC07 | Tutor Discovery & Q\&A | Guest, Parent, Tutor | View Public Profile | Displays the public view of a profile (UC05). Guests and parents view tutor profiles (posts, ratings); tutors view the short public profile of a parent who posted a request or sent an invitation. |
| UC08 | Tutor Discovery & Q\&A | Tutor | Manage Tutor Posts | Allows a tutor to create, update, hide and delete teaching advertisement posts. |
| UC09 | Tutor Discovery & Q\&A | Parent | View AI Tutor Suggestions | Recommends the most suitable tutors for a parent's tutoring request with an AI-generated explanation. |
| UC12 | Connection & Matching | Parent | Manage Tutoring Requests | Allows a parent to create, edit, close and re-open tutoring requests and to view, for each request, the list of tutors who clicked "Apply for Request". |
| UC13 | Connection & Matching | Tutor | Browse Requests & AI Post Suggestions | Allows a tutor to browse open tutoring requests with filters and receive AI-ranked requests that fit the tutor's profile. |
| UC14 | Connection & Matching | Tutor | apply for reques  | Allows a tutor to click "Interested" on an open request with a short note; requires at least one connection credit (no credit is spent yet). |
| UC15 | Connection & Matching | Parent | Respond to request application | Allows a parent to choose "Continue" or "Skip" for each interested tutor. "Continue" opens a 1-1 conversation and deducts one credit from the tutor. |
| UC16 | Connection & Matching | Parent | Invite Tutor | Allows a parent to invite a tutor (from search, profile or AI suggestions) to a tutoring request. Inviting is free for the parent. |
| UC17 | Connection & Matching | Tutor | Respond to Invitation | Allows a tutor to choose "Continue" (one credit is deducted and a 1-1 conversation opens) or "Skip" for a parent's invitation. |
| UC18 | Connection & Matching | Parent, Tutor | Confirm Connection | Optional "Agreed" confirmation after the two sides have talked (in-app chat or Zalo). When both confirm, the request is closed, rating is enabled and the tutor is suggested to create a classroom. |
| UC19 | Plans & Credits | Tutor | Upgrade Plan & Buy Credits | Allows a tutor to buy connection credits or upgrade from Free to Pro (more credits per month, higher AI quota, SMS reminders) via the Payment Gateway. |
| UC20 | Plans & Credits | Tutor | View Credits & Transactions | Shows the tutor's current plan, credit balance, credit usage per conversation and payment history with receipts. |
| UC21 | Classroom Workspace | Tutor | Create Classroom | Optional: only a tutor can create a classroom (basic classroom is free). The system generates an invite link, a join code and a class group chat. |
| UC22 | Classroom Workspace | Tutor | Manage Classroom | Allows a tutor to update class information, post announcements, regenerate the invite link/code, archive or delete a classroom. |
| UC23 | Classroom Workspace | Tutor | Manage Class Members | Allows a tutor to share the invite link/code, view and remove student and parent members, and see parent–student links. |
| UC24 | Classroom Workspace | Student, Parent | Join Classroom | Allows a student or a parent to join a classroom through the invite link or join code; a parent can link the child who is in the class. |
| UC25 | Classroom Workspace | Tutor | Manage Learning Materials | Allows a tutor to upload, organise, update and delete learning materials for a class. |
| UC26 | Classroom Workspace | Tutor | Manage Assignments & Grading | Allows a tutor to generate assignments with AI or create them manually (multiple choice, short answer, file upload), edit any question, publish with a deadline, grade short-answer/file items, give feedback and publish results to students and parents. |
| UC27 | Classroom Workspace | Student | Do Assignment | Allows a student to do an assignment on the web: answer MCQ (auto-graded), short-answer questions and upload files, then view score and feedback. |
| UC28 | Schedule & Reminders | Tutor | Manage Class Schedule | Allows a tutor to create one-off or recurring sessions, reschedule, cancel and mark attendance. Reminders are sent by email (Free) and SMS (Pro). |
| UC29 | Schedule & Reminders | Student, Parent | Request Schedule Change | Allows a student or parent to request moving or cancelling a session, proposing a new time and a reason. |
| UC30 | Schedule & Reminders | Tutor | Respond to Schedule Change Request | Allows a tutor to approve (session updated, calendar synced, members notified) or reject a schedule change request with a reason. |
| UC31 | Schedule & Reminders | Tutor, Student, Parent | Connect Google Calendar | Allows a user to link a Google account so that class sessions are synchronised to Google Calendar. |
| UC32 | Schedule & Reminders | Tutor, Student, Parent | View Schedule | Displays sessions in day/week/month views for the user's classes (parents see their children's sessions). |
| UC33 | Communication | Tutor | Create Group Chat | Allows a tutor to create group chats and manage members; a class group is auto-created with each classroom. |
| UC34 | Communication | Parent, Tutor, Student | Send & Receive Messages | Real-time 1-1 and group messaging. A parent–tutor 1-1 conversation exists only after a "Continue" (UC15/UC17); users may share Zalo/phone inside it. |
| UC35 | Communication | Parent, Tutor, Student, Admin | View Notifications | In-app, email and (Pro) SMS notifications about interests, invitations, conversations, sessions, schedule changes, assignments and results. |
| UC36 | Dashboard & Feedback | Student | View Student Dashboard | Shows joined classes, upcoming sessions, pending assignments, scores and feedback. |
| UC37 | Dashboard & Feedback | Parent | Monitor Child Progress | Allows a parent to follow each linked child's attendance, assignment scores, tutor feedback and schedule. |
| UC38 | Dashboard & Feedback | Parent | Submit Feedback & Rating | Allows a parent to rate (1–5 stars) and review a tutor once per connection, at any time after the connection is confirmed (UC18). |
| UC39 | Administration | Admin | Manage User Accounts | Allows Admin to search, view, lock/unlock user accounts. |
| UC40 | Administration | Admin | Moderate Content & Reports | Allows Admin to review flagged posts, requests, feedback, messages and user reports, then hide/remove content or warn/lock users. |
| UC41 | Administration | Admin | Manage Plans & Pricing | Allows Admin to configure Free/Pro plans, monthly credits, credit packs and prices, AI quota per plan and SMS reminder availability. |
| UC42 | Administration | Admin | View System Statistics | Dashboard with KPIs: users by role, requests, conversations opened, confirmed connections, credit revenue, active classes, AI usage. |

Table 4\. Use case list (42 use cases)

## **3\. Main Workflows**

### **3.1 WF-01: Tutor – Parent Connection**

The core connection flow. A parent posts a tutoring request; the system publishes it, shows AI tutor suggestions to the parent and AI post suggestions to tutors. A tutor clicks "Interested", or the parent invites a tutor for free. The receiving side chooses Continue or Skip. On Continue, one credit is deducted from the tutor (who can buy credits or upgrade to Pro) and a 1-1 conversation opens, where both sides can share Zalo or phone. Marking the connection as "Agreed" is optional; when both sides confirm, the request is closed, rating is enabled and the tutor is suggested to create a classroom.

**Related use cases:** UC07, UC09, UC12–UC19, UC34

![][image10]

Figure 11\. WF-01: Tutor – Parent Connection

### **3.2 WF-02: Classroom Setup & Scheduling**

The optional workspace flow. Only the tutor creates a classroom (a basic class is free); the system generates an invite link, a join code and a class group chat. Students and parents join through the link or code. The tutor schedules sessions with conflict checking and Google Calendar synchronisation; reminders are sent by email (Free) and SMS (Pro). Students or parents can request a schedule change, which the tutor approves or rejects.

**Related use cases:** UC21, UC23, UC24, UC28–UC33, UC35

![][image11]

Figure 12\. WF-02: Classroom Setup & Scheduling

### **3.3 WF-03: Assignment, Grading & Progress Monitoring**

The assignment loop. The tutor generates an assignment with AI (within the plan's AI quota) or creates it manually, edits the questions (multiple choice, short answer, file upload) and publishes it. Students do the assignment on the web; multiple-choice items are graded automatically and the tutor grades the rest. Results go to the student and parent dashboards, and the parent can rate the tutor once, at any time after the connection is confirmed.

**Related use cases:** UC26, UC27, UC36–UC38

![][image12]

Figure 13\. WF-03: Assignment, Grading

Data-level rules: Parents query/update only their own requests, contracts and linked children; Tutors only their own profile, posts, applications, classrooms and earnings; Students only classes they joined and their own submissions; Admin can query all data but can only change account status, verification, moderation and settings (all actions audited – BR-20).

*Table 6\. Screen authorization (X \= allowed)*

### **4.4 Non-UI Functions**

| \# | Feature | System Function | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | Notification | Notification Service | Pushes real-time in-app notifications via WebSocket (SignalR/Socket.IO) and sends emails through the Email Service according to user preferences. |
| 2 | Matching | Matching Engine | Scores tutor–request pairs (subject, grade, mode, area, schedule overlap, budget fit, rating, response rate). Produces Tutor Suggestions for parents and Student Suggestions for tutors; calls the AI Provider for natural-language explanations. |
| 3 | Payment | Payment Webhook (IPN) Handler | Receives Payment Gateway callbacks, verifies checksum and amount, updates the order idempotently, activates contracts, computes commission and tutor earnings. |
| 4 | Schedule | Google Calendar Sync Worker | Queues calendar create/update/delete jobs, refreshes OAuth tokens, retries failed syncs with back-off. |
| 5 | Scheduler | Expiry Jobs (cron) | Every 5 min: expire pending payment orders (15 min). Hourly: expire hire requests (48 h). Daily: expire tutoring requests (30 days). |
| 6 | Scheduler | Session Reminder Job | Sends reminders 24 h and 30 min before each session; generates weekly progress digests for parents. |
| 7 | Moderation | Content Filter | Checks text for prohibited words, phone numbers, emails and links; masks contact information (BR-19) and flags items (BR-22). |
| 8 | AI | AI Gateway | Central wrapper for the AI Provider: prompt templates, context building, quota enforcement, safety filter, streaming, logging and cost tracking. |
| 9 | Storage | File Storage Service | Uploads files to cloud storage, validates type/size, generates signed URLs for private documents (tutor credentials). |
| 10 | Security | Audit Logging | Records Admin actions and security events (login failures, invalid payment callbacks). |

*Table 7\. Non-UI functions*

## **5\. Business Rules**

| ID | Rule | Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-01 | Account & password | Email must be unique. Password: 8–64 characters with at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter and one digit. Phone: Vietnamese format (10 digits starting with 0). |
| BR-02 | Login lockout | After 5 consecutive failed logins the account is temporarily locked for 15 minutes. |
| BR-03 | One-time tokens | Verification and reset-password links/OTP are single-use and valid for 15 minutes (verification: 24 hours). |
| BR-04 | Verified tutors | Only tutors with status Verified appear in search/suggestions, can publish posts, apply to requests and receive hire requests. |
| BR-05 | Tutoring request | A request must include subject, grade, mode (online/offline), area (if offline), preferred schedule, sessions/week and budget/session. An Open request expires automatically after 30 days. Max 5 open requests per parent. |
| BR-06 | Applications | A tutor can apply only once per request and have at most 10 Pending applications at a time. |
| BR-07 | Hire request expiry | A hire request not answered within 48 hours is automatically Expired. |
| BR-08 | Contract activation | A contract becomes Active only after the first payment is confirmed by the Payment Gateway IPN. |
| BR-09 | Commission | Platform commission \= configurable % of each payment (default 10%). Tutor net earning \= amount − commission. |
| BR-10 | Payment orders | All amounts are in VND. Each order has a unique order code (idempotent processing). A pending order expires after 15 minutes. |
| BR-11 | Feedback eligibility | Only a parent with a contract that has at least one completed session can rate the tutor; one feedback per contract, rating 1–5, editable within 7 days. |
| BR-12 | Classroom | Join code: 6–8 alphanumeric characters, unique, regenerable. Default capacity 50 students (configurable by Admin). |
| BR-14 | Sessions | A tutor cannot have overlapping sessions. Changes are synchronised to Google Calendar within 1 minute when connected; reminders are sent 24 hours and 30 minutes before a session. |
| BR-15 | Assignments | Submissions after the deadline are marked Late and accepted only if the tutor enabled late submission. |
| BR-16 | Files | Max 20 MB per file (avatar 5 MB). Allowed: pdf, doc/docx, ppt/pptx, xls/xlsx, jpg, png, mp4, zip. |
| BR-17 | AI usage | Each tutor has a daily AI quota (default 50 requests, configurable). AI output is a draft; tutors must review before publishing to students. Failed AI calls do not consume quota. |
| BR-18 | Chat permission | Only members can read/send in a group. A 1-1 chat between a parent and a tutor is allowed only when a relation exists (question, application, hire request or contract). |
| BR-19 | Contact protection | Tutor/parent phone numbers and emails are hidden and auto-masked in messages/answers until a contract between them is Active. |
| BR-20 | Admin audit | Every Admin action (lock, approve/reject, remove content, change settings) requires a reason and is written to the audit log. |
| BR-22 | Content filter | Posts, requests, feedback and messages containing prohibited words, phone numbers or external links are flagged for moderation. |

*Table 8\. Business rules*

## **6\. Non-Functional Requirements**

| Category | Requirement |
| ----- | ----- |
| Performance | 95% of API requests respond within 2 seconds under 500 concurrent users; chat messages delivered within 1 second; AI responses start streaming within 5 seconds. |
| Availability | System uptime ≥ 99% per month excluding planned maintenance (announced 24 h ahead). |
| Security | HTTPS/TLS everywhere; passwords hashed with BCrypt; JWT access token 30 min \+ refresh token 7 days; role-based authorization on every API; OAuth tokens and credentials encrypted at rest; payment callbacks verified by checksum; OWASP Top 10 mitigations. |
| Privacy | Personal data processed according to Vietnam Decree 13/2023/ND-CP on personal data protection; tutor documents accessible only to the owner and Admin; contact info protected (BR-19). |
| Usability | Responsive web UI (desktop, tablet, mobile ≥ 360 px); Vietnamese and English UI; main tasks achievable within 3 clicks from the dashboard. |
| Scalability | Stateless API behind a load balancer; background jobs in a queue; files in object storage. |
| Maintainability | Layered/modular architecture per package; code coverage of business services ≥ 60%; API documented with Swagger/OpenAPI. |
| Compatibility | Latest 2 versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari. |
| Reliability | Daily database backup kept 14 days; idempotent payment processing; retry with back-off for external APIs. |

*Table 9\. Non-functional requirements*

| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: The guest is not logged in. PRE-2: The guest has a valid email address. |  |  |

| **Normal Flow:** | **UC01.0 Register Account** 1\. Guest opens the Register screen. 2\. System displays the registration form and role selection (Parent / Tutor / Student). 3\. Guest enters full name, email, phone, password, confirm password and selects a role. 4\. Guest agrees to the Terms of Service and clicks "Register". 5\. System validates the data (BR-01) and checks email uniqueness. 6\. System creates the account, sends a verification link by email and shows a success message. 7\. Guest clicks the link in the email; System activates the account and redirects to Login. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | **A1: Register with Google** 1\. Guest clicks "Continue with Google". 2\. System redirects to Google OAuth; Guest grants consent. 3\. System receives the Google profile, asks the guest to choose a role and creates an Active account. 4\. System logs the user in and redirects to the role dashboard. **A2: Tutor registration** 1\. If the role is Tutor, after activation System redirects to Manage Profile (UC05) to complete the teaching profile (subjects, grade levels, hourly rate, availability). |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | **E1: Invalid or missing data** → System highlights invalid fields with messages (e.g. "Password must be at least 8 characters"). Return to step 3\. **E2: Email already used** → System shows "This email is already registered" and offers "Login" / "Forgot password". **E3: Verification link expired** → System shows "Link expired" and offers "Resend verification email". |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | Once per user. |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | BR-01: Account & password; BR-03: One-time tokens |  |  |
| **Screens:** | SC03 – Register |  |  |

| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: The parent is logged in. PRE-2: The parent has at least one Open tutoring request (UC12). |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1: A ranked list (top 10\) of tutors with a match score and reason is shown and cached for 24 hours. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **UC09.0 View AI Tutor Suggestions** 1\. Parent selects a tutoring request and clicks "AI Suggestions". 2\. System filters tutors by hard constraints (subject, grade, mode, area). 3\. System computes a match score (schedule overlap, budget fit, rating, response rate). 4\. System sends the top candidates and request summary to the AI Provider to generate a short explanation per tutor. 5\. System displays the ranked list with score, reason and an "Invite" button (UC16). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | **A1: Refine** 1\. Parent adjusts weights (e.g. price vs. rating) and clicks "Refresh"; System recalculates. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | **E1: AI Provider unavailable/timeout** → System shows the rule-based ranking without AI explanations and logs the error. **E2: No candidate** → System suggests widening criteria and notifies the parent when a matching tutor registers. |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | Per request. |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | BR-17: AI usage |  |  |
| **Screens:** | SC18 – AI Tutor Suggestions |  |  |

System validates (BR-05), runs the content filter (BR-22) and publishes the request. 5\. System runs matching and shows AI tutor suggestions (UC09). 6\. Parent opens "My Tutoring Requests"; System lists the requests with status and the number of interested tutors. 7\. Parent opens a request; System shows the "Interested tutors" list (tutor card, note, match score) where the parent can choose Continue or Skip (UC15). |  |  |

Parent clicks "Save draft"; System stores it without publishing. **A3: Request closed by connection** 1\. When a connection on this request is confirmed (UC18), System closes the request automatically. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | **E1: Missing mandatory fields** → System highlights the fields. **E2: More than 5 open requests** → System asks the parent to close an existing request first (BR-05). |  |  |

| **Created By:** | Chiến | **Date Created:** | 29/09/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | Tutor | **Secondary Actors:** | Payment Gateway |
| **Trigger:** | Tutor clicks "Upgrade" / "Buy credits" on the dashboard, or is redirected from UC14 / UC15 / UC17 when credits run out. |  |  |
| **Description:** | Allows a tutor to buy a credit pack or upgrade from the Free plan to the Pro plan (more connection credits per month, higher AI quota, SMS reminders) and pay through the Payment Gateway. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: The tutor is logged in. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1: After a valid payment result, the plan is upgraded or the credits are added and a receipt is stored (UC20). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **UC19.0 Upgrade Plan & Buy Credits** 1\. System shows the plans (Free, Pro) and credit packs with prices configured by Admin (UC41). 2\. Tutor selects the Pro plan (monthly) or a credit pack and clicks "Checkout". 3\. System creates a payment order (BR-10) and redirects the tutor to the Payment Gateway. 4\. Tutor pays by QR / ATM card / credit card. 5\. Payment Gateway returns the result (redirect \+ IPN). 6\. System verifies the IPN signature, upgrades the plan or adds the credits and shows the Payment Result screen. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | **A1: Auto-renew Pro** 1\. Before the period ends, System reminds the tutor; the tutor renews with the same flow or the plan returns to Free. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | **E1: Payment failed or cancelled** → System shows the failure and allows retrying; nothing is changed. **E2: Invalid IPN signature / duplicate order** → System ignores the request and logs it (BR-10). |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | Monthly. |  |  |
| **zBusiness Rules:** | BR-10: Payment orders; Plans: Free (5 credits/month, basic classroom, email reminders); Pro (30 credits/month, higher AI quota, SMS reminders) |  |  |
| **Screens:** | SC20 – Checkout; SC21 – Payment Result |  |  |

#### ***a. Screen Design***

| UC ID and Name: | UC26 – Manage Assignments & Grading |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |

| **Primary Actor:** | Tutor | **Secondary Actors:** | AI Provider |
| **Trigger:** | Tutor opens the "Assignments" tab of a classroom. |  |  |
| **Description:** | Allows a tutor to generate an assignment with AI or create it manually, with three question types (multiple choice, short answer, file upload). The tutor can edit every question, publish with a deadline, grade short-answer and file items, give feedback and publish the results to students and parents. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: The tutor owns the classroom with at least one student. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1: The assignment is published and students are notified; results are visible to students and linked parents. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **UC26.0 Manage Assignments & Grading** 1\. Tutor clicks "New assignment" and chooses "Generate with AI". 2\. Tutor enters topic, grade, difficulty, number of questions and question types. 3\. System checks the AI quota of the tutor's plan (BR-17) and sends the request to the AI Provider. 4\. System shows the generated questions as an editable draft. 5\. Tutor edits, deletes or adds questions, sets the answer key, points, deadline and late policy. 6\. Tutor clicks "Publish"; System notifies the students. 7\. After submissions (UC27), System auto-grades multiple-choice items. 8\. Tutor grades short-answer and file items and writes feedback. 9\. Tutor clicks "Publish results"; System updates student and parent dashboards and notifies them. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | **A1: Create manually** 1\. Tutor chooses "Create manually" and adds questions of the three types without AI (steps 2–4 are skipped). **A2: Override auto-grade** 1\. Tutor changes the score of an auto-graded item with a comment. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | **E1: AI quota used up / AI timeout** → System informs the tutor, suggests upgrading (UC19) and keeps the manual editor. **E2: Deadline in the past or no answer key for MCQ** → System shows a validation message. |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | Weekly. |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | BR-15: Assignments; BR-17: AI usage (quota depends on plan) |  |  |
| **Screens:** | SC33 – Classroom Detail (Tutor); SC34 – Assignment Grading |  |  |

| UC ID and Name: | UC28 – Manage Class Schedule |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Created By:** | Nghĩa | **Date Created:** | 29/09/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | Tutor | **Secondary Actors:** | Google Calendar API, Email / SMS Service |
| **Trigger:** | Tutor opens the "Schedule" tab of a classroom or the global Calendar. |  |  |
| **Description:** | Allows a tutor to create one-off or recurring sessions (time, duration, online link/location), reschedule, cancel and mark attendance. Changes are pushed to Google Calendar when connected. Reminders are sent by email (Free plan) and by SMS (Pro plan). |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: The tutor owns the classroom. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1: Sessions are saved; members are notified; Google Calendar events are created/updated; reminders are scheduled (BR-14). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **UC28.0 Manage Class Schedule** 1\. Tutor clicks "Add session". 2\. Tutor enters date, start time, duration, repeat rule (weekly on selected days until end date), meeting link or address. 3\. System checks conflicts with the tutor's other sessions. 4\. System saves the sessions and notifies class members. 5\. If Google Calendar is connected, System sends calendar requests and stores the returned event IDs. 6\. System schedules reminders 24 hours and 30 minutes before each session: email for all members, SMS when the tutor has the Pro plan. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | **A1: Reschedule / cancel session** 1\. Tutor changes or cancels a session with a reason (or approves a change request, UC30); System updates Google Calendar and notifies members. **A2: Mark attendance** 1\. After the session, tutor marks Present/Absent/Late for each student; data feeds the dashboards. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | **E1: Time conflict** → System shows the conflicting session and blocks saving. **E2: Google Calendar error / token expired** → System saves locally, marks sync Pending and asks the tutor to reconnect (UC31). |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | Weekly. |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | BR-14: Sessions |  |  |
| **Screens:** | SC13 – Calendar; SC33 – Classroom Detail (Tutor) |  |  |

| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: The user is a member of the class (a parent through the linked child). PRE-2: The session has not started yet. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1: A schedule change request with status Pending is created and the tutor is notified. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **UC29.0 Request Schedule Change** 1\. User selects a session and clicks "Request change". 2\. System shows the form: type (move / cancel), proposed date and time, reason. 3\. System saves the request (Pending) and notifies the tutor. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | **A1: Withdraw request** 1\. User withdraws a Pending request; System notifies the tutor. |  |  |

| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: A Pending schedule change request exists for one of the tutor's sessions. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1 (Approve): The session is moved or cancelled, calendar events are updated and reminders are rescheduled. POST-2 (Reject): The request is Rejected and the requester is notified with the reason. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **UC30.0 Respond to Schedule Change Request** 1\. Tutor opens the request and sees the session, proposed time and reason. 2\. Tutor clicks "Approve" (optionally adjusts the time). 3\. System checks for conflicts with the tutor's other sessions. 4\. System updates the session, synchronises Google Calendar (if connected) and reschedules the reminders. 5\. System notifies the requester and all class members. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | **A1: Reject** 1\. Tutor clicks "Reject" and enters a reason; System notifies the requester. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | **E1: Time conflict** → System shows the conflicting session and asks the tutor to choose another time. **E2: Google Calendar error** → System saves the change, marks sync Pending and asks the tutor to reconnect (UC31). |  |  |
| **Priority:** | Medium |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | Occasional. |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | BR-14: Sessions |  |  |

# **III. System Design**

## **1\. Package Diagram**

TuConnector follows a layered (clean) architecture. The front-end SPA is split into feature packages matching the functional packages of Section II. The back-end separates API, application (business services), domain, data access and integration layers; background jobs reuse the application services. Dependencies point downward only.

![drawio/package.png][image61]

*Figure 18\. TuConnector package diagram*

| Package | Description / responsibilities |
| ----- | ----- |
| Presentation (Web SPA) | React (Vite) \+ TypeScript, TailwindCSS. Feature folders: auth, discovery, hiring, payment, classroom, schedule, chat, ai, dashboard, admin; shared components, API client, WebSocket client. |
| API Layer | REST controllers per module, SignalR/WebSocket hubs (chat, notification), webhook endpoints (payment IPN), authentication & authorization middleware, validation, Swagger. |
| Application / Business Layer | Services per module: AuthService, ProfileService, DiscoveryService, HiringService, MatchingService, PaymentService, ClassroomService, ScheduleService, ChatService, NotificationService, AIAssistantService, DashboardService, AdminService; DTOs and mappers. |
| Domain Layer | Entities, enums, business rules (BR-xx), domain events (ContractActivated, SessionChanged…). |
| Data Access Layer | ORM (EF Core / Prisma) DbContext, repositories, migrations, unit of work. |
| Integration Layer | Adapters: GeminiClient (AI Provider), PaymentGatewayClient (PayOS/VNPay), GoogleCalendarClient, GoogleOAuthClient, EmailSender, FileStorageClient. |
| Background Jobs | Scheduler/queue (Hangfire / BullMQ): expiry jobs, reminders, calendar sync, email sending, matching recalculation. |
| Cross-cutting | Logging, audit log, caching (Redis), configuration, exception handling, security utilities. |

*Table 10\. Package descriptions*

**Mapping of functional packages to code packages:**

| Functional package | Front-end / back-end packages |
| ----- | ----- |
| Authentication & Account | auth / AuthService, ProfileService, GoogleOAuthClient, EmailSender |
| Tutor Discovery & Q\&A | discovery / DiscoveryService, MatchingService, GeminiClient |
| Hiring & Matching | hiring / HiringService, MatchingService |
| Payment | payment / PaymentService, PaymentGatewayClient, Webhooks |
| Classroom Workspace | classroom / ClassroomService, FileStorageClient |
| Schedule & Calendar | schedule / ScheduleService, GoogleCalendarClient, Calendar Sync Worker |
| Communication | chat / ChatService, NotificationService, Hubs |
| AI Assistant | ai-assistant / AIAssistantService, GeminiClient |
| Dashboard & Feedback | dashboard / DashboardService |
| Administration | admin / AdminService, Logging & Audit |

## **2\. Database Design**

### **2.1 Entity-Relationship Diagram**

The full ERD (all 33 tables, keys only) is shown first; because of its size it is also split into three readable parts by domain. Entities drawn with a dashed border are references to tables detailed in another part. Crow's-foot notation: \|\| \= exactly one, o\| \= zero or one, o\< \= zero or many.

![drawio/erd.png][image62]

*Figure 19\. Entity-Relationship Diagram*

### **2.2 Table Descriptions**

| No | Table | Description | Attributes |
| :---: | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **1** | ROLE | Lookup of user roles (STUDENT, PARENT, TUTOR, ADMIN). | role\_id (PK), role\_name (UK) |
| **2** | USERS | Shared user account: login credentials, role and account status. | user\_id (PK), full\_name, email (UK), phone, password\_hash, email\_verify\_status, role\_id (FK), is\_onboarded, created\_at, account\_status, failed\_login\_attempts, last\_login\_at, updated\_at, has\_password, avatar\_url, is\_looked |
| **3** | GOOGLE\_ACCOUNTS | Links a user account to a Google account (OAuth login). | google\_id (PK), user\_id (FK, UK), google\_email |
| **4** | VERIFICATION\_TOKENS | Tokens/OTPs used to verify an email address. | token\_id (PK), user\_id (FK), token\_value (UK), expired\_at, is\_used |
| **5** | USER\_SESSIONS | Login sessions, storing the refresh token and revocation status. | session\_id (PK), user\_id (FK), refresh\_token (UK), is\_revoked, expires\_at |
| **6** | PASSWORD\_RESET\_TOKENS | Tokens used to reset a password. | token\_id (PK), user\_id (FK), token\_value, expired\_at, is\_used |
| **7** | USER\_CALENDAR\_TOKENS | Tokens connecting a user's personal calendar (Google Calendar). | token\_id (PK), user\_id (FK, UK), provider, access\_token, refresh\_token, google\_calendar\_id, is\_connected, last\_synced\_at, expires\_at |
| **8** | TUTOR\_PROFILES | Tutor profile: introduction, address, availability and average rating. | profile\_id (PK), user\_id (FK, UK), headline, bio, avatar\_url, cover\_url, address, is\_address\_hidden, is\_complete, is\_available, average\_rating |
| **9** | EXPERIENCES | Work experience of a tutor. | exp\_id (PK), profile\_id (FK), title, company, start\_date |
| **10** | ACHIEVEMENTS | Achievements and awards of a tutor. | ach\_id (PK), profile\_id (FK), title, description |
| **11** | EDUCATIONS | Education and degrees of a tutor. | edu\_id (PK), profile\_id (FK), school, degree, graduation\_year, description |
| **12** | TUTOR\_CREDITS | Current credit balance of a tutor. | credit\_id (PK), tutor\_profile\_id (FK, UK), balance, updated\_at |
| **13** | CREDIT\_TRANSACTIONS | History of a tutor's credit changes (top-up, deduction, refund, bonus). | transaction\_id (PK), tutor\_profile\_id (FK), amount, type, related\_request\_id (FK), expires\_at, created\_at |
| **14** | REVIEWS | Parent reviews of a tutor, with sub-ratings, the tutor's reply and moderation status. | review\_id (PK), tutor\_profile\_id (FK), parent\_user\_id (FK), connection\_id, rating, comment, knowledge\_rating, punctuality\_rating, communication\_rating, tutor\_reply, replied\_at, status, created\_at, updated\_at |
| **15** | TUTOR\_POSTS | Posts in which a tutor offers teaching services. | post\_id (PK), profile\_id (FK), title, subject\_name, grade\_level, teaching\_mode, price, schedule, description, image\_urls, status, created\_at, updated\_at |
| **16** | PARENT\_REQUESTS | Requests posted by parents to find a tutor (subject, budget, schedule, tutor requirements). | request\_id (PK), parent\_user\_id (FK), title, subject\_name, grade\_level, teaching\_mode, budget, schedule, description, location\_address, image\_urls, status, student\_id, tutor\_requirements, created\_at, updated\_at |
| **17** | INTERESTED\_TUTORS | Tutors who expressed interest in a parent's request, with a match score. | interest\_id (PK), request\_id (FK), tutor\_profile\_id (FK), note, match\_score, status, created\_at, updated\_at |
| **18** | BOOKMARKED\_REQUESTS | Parent requests saved by tutors. | bookmark\_id (PK), tutor\_profile\_id (FK), request\_id (FK), created\_at |
| **19** | TUTOR\_INVITATIONS | Invitations sent by a parent to a tutor for a request. | invitation\_id (PK), parent\_user\_id (FK), tutor\_profile\_id (FK), request\_id (FK), message, status, created\_at, updated\_at |
| **20** | CONNECTIONS | Agreement between a parent and a tutor (agreed subject, schedule and tuition). | connection\_id (PK), request\_id (FK), parent\_user\_id (FK), tutor\_profile\_id (FK), agreed\_subject, agreed\_schedule, agreed\_price, status, created\_at, updated\_at |
| **21** | CLASSROOMS | Online classes created by tutors, with a join code and invite link. | class\_id (PK), tutor\_profile\_id (FK), connection\_id (FK), name, subject, grade, description, capacity, join\_code (UK), invite\_link (UK), status, created\_at, updated\_at |
| **22** | CLASS\_MEMBERS | Members of a class and their roles in it. | member\_id (PK), class\_id (FK), user\_id (FK), role, joined\_at, student\_user\_id (FK), status, removal\_reason |
| **23** | CLASS\_ANNONCEMENTS | Class announcements posted by the tutor, which can be pinned. | announcement\_id (PK), class\_id (FK), author\_profile\_id (FK), content, is\_pinned, created\_at, updated\_at |
| **24** | MATERIAL\_TOPICS | Topics used to group materials within a class. | topic\_id (PK), class\_id (FK), name, created\_at |
| **25** | CLASS\_MATERIALS | Learning materials of a class (documents, videos, links, assignments). | material\_id (PK), class\_id (FK), topic\_id (FK), uploader\_profile\_id (FK), title, material\_type, file\_url, file\_size, visibility, created\_at, updated\_at |
| **26** | ASSIGNMENTS | Class assignments: due date, maximum points, late/resubmission rules, AI-generated flag. | assignment\_id (PK), class\_id (FK), creator\_profile\_id (FK), title, instructions, is\_ai\_generated, status, due\_date, allow\_late\_submission, allow\_resubmission, total\_points, published\_at, results\_published\_at, created\_at, updated\_at |
| **27** | ASSIGNMENT\_QUESTIONS | Questions of an assignment (multiple choice, essay, short answer). | question\_id (PK), assignment\_id (FK), question\_number, question\_type, content, options, correct\_answer, points |
| **28** | ASSIGNMENT\_SUBMISSIONS | A student's submission for an assignment, with scores and feedback. | submission\_id (PK), assignment\_id (FK), student\_user\_id (FK), attempt\_number, status, submission\_type, provisional\_score, final\_score, overall\_feedback, submitted\_at, graded\_at |
| **29** | SUBMISSION\_ANSWERS | A student's detailed answer to each question, with score and comment. | answer\_id (PK), submission\_id (FK), question\_id (FK), text\_response, file\_url, file\_size, score, is\_auto\_graded, is\_overridden, comment |
| **30** | ASSIGNMENT\_ATTACHMENTS | Links assignments to attached materials. | attachment\_id (PK), assignment\_id (FK), material\_id (FK) |
| **31** | RECURRING\_RULES | Rules for recurring class schedules (days of week, start time, duration, end date). | rule\_id (PK), class\_id (FK), days\_of\_week, start\_time, duration\_minutes, end\_date |
| **32** | CLASS\_SESSIONS | Individual class sessions: time, meeting link and status. | session\_id (PK), class\_id (FK), tutor\_profile\_id (FK), rule\_id (FK), title, start\_time, end\_time, meeting\_link, status, created\_at, updated\_at |
| **33** | SESSION\_ATTENDANCE | Student attendance for each session. | attendance\_id (PK), session\_id (FK), student\_user\_id (FK), status, comment, marked\_at |
| **34** | SCHEDULE\_CHANGE\_REQUESTS | Requests to reschedule or cancel a session, and the responses. | request\_id (PK), session\_id (FK), requester\_user\_id (FK), responder\_user\_id (FK), request\_type, proposed\_start\_time, proposed\_end\_time, reason, status, response\_comment, responded\_at, created\_at |
| **35** | SESSION\_REMINDERS | Session reminders sent by email, SMS or push. | reminder\_id (PK), session\_id (FK), user\_id (FK), channel, trigger\_time, scheduled\_for, status, sent\_at |
| **36** | SESSION\_CALENDAR\_SYNC | Sync status of a session to a user's Google Calendar. | sync\_id (PK), session\_id (FK), user\_id (FK), google\_event\_id, sync\_status, last\_error, synced\_at |
| **37** | MESSAGES | Messages within a conversation. | message\_id (PK), conversation\_id (FK), sender\_user\_id (FK), message\_type, content, created\_at |
| **38** | MESSAGE\_ATTACHMENTS | Files attached to messages. | attachment\_id (PK), message\_id (FK), file\_url, file\_name, file\_size, mime\_type |
| **39** | CONVERSATION\_READ\_STATES | Per-user read state of messages in a conversation. | state\_id (PK), conversation\_id (FK), user\_id (FK), last\_read\_message\_id, read\_at |
| **40** | MESSAGE\_REPORTS | Reports of violations against a message. | report\_id (PK), message\_id (FK), reporter\_user\_id (FK), reason, status, created\_at |
| **41** | CONTENT\_REPORTS | General content violation reports (posts, requests, reviews, messages, users, classes) and the admin's resolution. | report\_id (PK), reporter\_user\_id (FK), target\_type, target\_id, reason, severity, status, action\_taken, admin\_note, resolved\_by\_admin\_id (FK), resolved\_at, created\_at |

| **46** | ADMIN\_AUDIT\_LOGS | Audit log of administrator actions. | log\_id (PK), admin\_user\_id (FK), target\_user\_id (FK), action, reason, details\_json, ip\_address, created\_at |
